:::{#def-channel-capacity}
#### Channel capacity

Send one input $X$ through a [discrete memoryless channel](#def-channel),
and let $Y$ be the output.
The joint distribution of $(X, Y)$ is
$\P(X = x, Y = y) = \P(X = x) \, p(y \mid x)$,
so the
[mutual information](entropy.qmd#def-mutual-information) $I(X; Y)$
depends on the channel and on the input distribution.
The **capacity** of the channel is the largest mutual information
any input distribution achieves:

$$C \eqdef \max_{\P(X = \cdot)} I(X; Y),$$

where the maximum runs over all probability mass functions on $\mathcal{X}$
[@cover2006elements, chapter 7].
With base-2 logarithms, $C$ is measured in *bits per channel use*.

:::
